spans.text: ...The Séance Room.
It is currently out of business hours. The candles are unlit in the vast and empty room.
Sitting cross-legged on the floor, Miss Séance swirls the cheap liquor in her glass.
...You remember everything I just told you?
Yes, would you like me to repeat it?
Nah.
Miss Séance takes a sip from her glass and savors the spiciness of the liquor.
Little surprises are what makes séances so eerie and enthralling...
I understand. I will watch your cues and act accordingly.
Splendid. Then I'll be counting on you, Miss Poker.
Miss Séance stows her wine glass away and swaggers up to the door. She lights the candles along the way.
Oh, right.
Do you have any further instructions for me?
Miss Séance turns around and winks at her mischievously.
Don't tell the Mistresses about my drinking.
Understood.
Creak...
While Miss Séance is away getting dressed and applying her makeup, Miss Poker conceals herself in the dark and waits silently for their customers of the day.
Several minutes later, the door opens again.
Miss Séance leads a sad woman into the candlelit room.
Please take a seat, madam.
Miss Séance shoots Miss Poker a look, telling her to get ready.
Is it... really possible to converse with the dead here?
Very much so.
What do I have to do?
Please place your index finger on this planchette.
The woman does as she is told and puts her finger on the planchette shaped like a teardrop. Miss Séance does the same.
She moves the planchette to the center of the ouija board away from all the numbers and letters on the ouija board.
Are you ready?
Do it...
I shall begin the séance then.
O wandering spirits, heed my heart and answer my summon...
Hearing her cue, Miss Poker throws a card—
Whoosh—the dim and flickering candlelight is extinguished.
Ah!
Don't be afraid. I need you to focus on saying the prayer with me.
You will only receive an answer if you pray with sincerity.
I... understand...
O wandering spirits, this lady's beloved has gone missing. Please heed her question...
Pose your question, Madam.
Please tell me, where is my beloved?
Squeak... squeak...
The planchette starts sliding slowly across the ouija board. As it moves from letter to letter, the answer soon becomes apparent.
"Not far"?
So your beloved is still close by.
Then how do I find him?!
Please direct your question reverently to the ouija board. Just so you know, I only have enough spiritual power for three questions.
Right...
Could you please tell me how I can find my beloved?
Squeak... squeak...
The planchette moves slowly across the ouija board again—
"Wait".
I've been waiting for so long, I'm starting to lose hope...
Will he really come back to me?
I don't even know if he still loves me...
Squeak... squeak...
The planchette slowly glides towards—
"Yes".
An answer in the affirmative.
Really...?
Despite the positive answer, the lady does not seem particularly comforted. She looks just as dejected as she did when she first entered the room.
Miss Séance glances at Miss Poker.
Madam, I can sense that the spirits in this room still have a message for you.
...What is it?
Miss Poker knows that she's up again.
Miss Séance has given her free rein over what to do in this part of the session, which means she gets to decide what response to give.
Miss Poker gazes at the woman's melancholic profile and looks down at her deck of cards...
Whoosh—
Oh, the spirits have offered a final hint.
A playing card shoots through the air and starts drifting slowly down from above the woman's head.
It lands in front of her like a nimble butterfly.
Queen of diamonds?
Madam, do you know the story of the queen of diamonds?
No. What story can a playing card have?
The woman depicted on the queen of diamonds is Rachel, a beautiful and hardworking young lady.
The spirits want me to... be like Rachel?
Please allow me to finish.
Rachel had a faithful lover, but her father would only allow him to marry her if he worked for him for seven years.
Seven years later, Rachel's father changed his mind again. He told Rachel's lover that he could marry Rachel in seven days, but only if he worked for him for another seven years.
Rachel's lover agreed and worked for Rachel's father for seven more years after marrying Rachel.
This Rachel was very lucky to have such a faithful lover.
Legend has it, Rachel and her lover remained in love throughout their lives, but I believe there must have been moments when they felt lost and hopeless.
Rachel chose to have faith in her lover and waited for him to make his choice.
Hm...
A glimmer of hope has been kindled in the woman's sad eyes.
I see. I will keep waiting and give him some more time.
Very well. Then let us conclude this séance.
We thank the spirits for giving us the answers we seek. Please return to your realm...
Squeak... squeak...
The planchette slowly glides towards "Goodbye".
...A few minutes later, Miss Séance returns to the Séance Room for a break after escorting the customer on her way out.
Miss Poker also comes out from the shadows and sits down on the cold floor like Miss Séance.
Oh my, another job well done.
You've really got talent. You did such a fantastic job the woman ended up spending quite a lot afterwards.
Miss Séance takes out her hidden wine glass and takes a cheerful sip.
Ah—that hit the spot!
Why are you being so quiet?
Why didn't you finish Rachel's story just now?
Ha... There was no need. Humans only ever want to hear what they want to hear.
These are customers looking to spend with us, so it is naturally our job to make them happy.
I understand. I'll remember that.
Miss Poker starts jotting it down solemnly.
Relax. You don't have to take everything so seriously.
I don't understand.
Hm?
As the Mistresses' Dolls, we are always at risk of being discarded. Are you not afraid, Miss Séance?
All Dolls are afraid of being abandoned.
Then why do you...
Miss Poker's gaze falls on the wine glass in Miss Séance's hand.
Oh, this? If you want to know, why don't you try it yourself?
Reflected in the low-quality liquor, Miss Séance's smile seems both dangerous and alluring.
Compelled by some unknown forces, Miss Poker reaches out to take the glass...
By the time Miss Poker comes to, it is already way past midnight.
She is lying in a repair pod; her neural cloud feels like it's been pulverized by a hundred hammers.
Hey, you're awake?
How... how long have I been sleeping?
About five hours? Or six? Maybe seven? Or eight?
Don't worry. Miss Séance told the Mistresses that you fell down the stairs and hit your head in your eagerness to do your job.
And they didn't say anything?
Obviously, or you'd have been sold off before you even woke up.
Miss Pachinko, who is in the middle of removing her makeup, suddenly stops what she's doing and sits down by Miss Poker's repair pod.
Hey, seeing that we're roommates, let me give you some friendly advice.
Yes?
Don't trust Miss Séance.
Why?
Miss Poker stares uncomprehendingly at Miss Pachinko's half-removed drawn-on eyebrow.
Why? Because she can't be trusted, duh!
From my experience of working with her, she seems quite dependable.
Then how did you end up in the repair pod?
It's my own f...
Miss Poker suddenly remembers what Miss Séance asked of her and stops talking mid-sentence.
After making sure none of the other Dolls in the dorm are listening in, Miss Pachinko leans forward and whispers conspiratorially into Miss Poker's ear.
Do you know about... Miss Séance's secret?
What secret?
Look around this house. All the Dolls in the Mistresses' employment are here.
But Miss Séance has never set foot in here.
I believe... she lives in the Séance Room. It is probably more convenient for her work.
Look at Miss Tourguide. She lives here even though her daily commute is three hours.
So what gives Miss Séance the right to live all by herself in the Séance Room, which is only a 15-minute walk from here?
Seeing that Miss Poker has nothing to say, Miss Pachinko bats the fake lashes still glued to her eyelids and lowers her voice.
As you know, the Dolls in this house have a really high turnover. We're always in danger of being thrown out...
I know.
I know that only too well.
But Miss Séance doesn't seem at all concerned about this. She has the Mistresses' trust...
Just think about it—why is she so favored?
Because she brings in a lot more profit than the rest of us?
Pfft.
Miss Pachinko scoffs in an exaggerated manner.
You're so naïve, Miss Poker.
This is Miss Séance's secret! It's hidden in her room.
How did she manage to win the Mistresses' trust... and get this kind of special treatment?
Don't you want to know? The secret trick that will save you from getting the boot...?
As the Mistresses' Dolls, we are always at risk of being discarded. Are you not afraid, Miss Séance?
All Dolls are afraid of being abandoned.
Then why do you...
Oh, this? If you want to know, why don't you try it yourself?
...I do want to know.
Gazing at Miss Pachinko's patchy makeup, Miss Poker replies softly.
I want to know...
I don't want to be discarded...
...A few days later, in the Séance Room.
After closing up for the day, Miss Séance and Miss Poker tidy up the room.
Good work as always!
See you tomorrow, Miss Poker.
As usual, Miss Séance walks Miss Poker out the door.
Yes, Miss Séance. See you tomorrow.
...A moment later, Miss Poker, who has been crouching outside and observing the room, climbs inside through the window.
Miss Séance?
The silent room is utterly still.
After making sure that Miss Séance isn't around, Miss Poker sneaks up the stairs and into a room on the second floor.
...Miss Séance's bedroom.
The lock is not at all secure; Miss Poker manages to dislodge it with just a playing card.
The room is only minimally furnished with a modest bed, a wooden chair, a small fridge, and a coffee table.
The floor is littered with liquor bottles.
Miss Poker peers over at Miss Séance, who is lying spread eagle on the bed, seemingly asleep.
After some thought, Miss Poker musters her courage and pushes open the door. She sits down by Miss Séance's bed.
Miss Séance... I'm very sorry for entering your room without your permission...
But I simply have too many questions. If I don't get any answers, I'm afraid they will affect our working relationship.
Miss Séance is still sound asleep.
Miss Séance? Please wake up...
Miss Poker taps Miss Séance lightly on the face, but she gives no reaction.
Miss Séance is usually very responsive, so this uncharacteristic lack of response is giving Miss Poker a very bad feeling.
She probingly inspects the status of her neural cloud and is surprised to find that Miss Séance has actually crashed.
What happened... Miss Séance?! Hang in there!
I'm taking you to the repair bay...
Miss Poker hoists the unconscious Miss Séance over her shoulders and trudges out the door with great difficulty.
...Standing at the top of the long flight of stairs, Miss Poker jostles Miss Séance's weight helplessly, not quite sure what to do.
I'm sorry, Miss Séance, I really can't carry you...
The only way I can bring you to the repair bay is this...
She carefully sets Miss Séance down on the stairs, then padding out her most vulnerable parts, she slowly drags her down the stairs...
Thunk, thunk, thunk...
Miss Séance's body produces a sharp clang as she lands on every stairstep.
What are you doing?!
You're finally awake! That's such a relief, Miss Séance! I was so worried you wouldn't wake up again...
In her relief, Miss Poker loosens her grip, and Miss Séance rolls down the last few steps and hits the floor.
Thunk!
Miss Séance finally comes to a stop with a crash.
It seems to me you're actively trying to make sure I never wake up again...
No! Your neural cloud crashed just now... I thought you had some kind of malfunction, so I wanted to take you to the repair bay...
How did you know my neural cloud crashed?
Miss Séance sits up cross-legged. Rubbing her sore crown, she peers at the flustered Miss Poker with some amusement.
I trespassed into your room. I'm sorry.
What were you doing in my room after hours?
Miss Poker sits down next to Miss Séance in silence.
I wanted to ask you some questions...
Let me guess... Someone's been talking?
...Yes.
Fetch me something to drink first. I'm all sore after you dragged me down the stairs.
Miss Poker runs off and comes back with a glass of liquor apologetically.
Ask away. What do you want to know?
I once asked you whether or not you're afraid of being abandoned by the Mistresses.
I want to know the reason why the Mistresses would not get rid of you...
Ha, you just saw it.
When?
Literally just now. My neural cloud crashed, right?
I was taking care of some business for the Mistresses, but I crashed for a bit because the processing load was too much.
If you're wondering what kind of business it was, then I'm afraid I can't tell you.
I see...
Miss Séance downs the liquor in one go and exhales in satisfaction. The spicy scent of alcohol instantly fills the air.
This is my so-called "secret".
Disappointed?
Miss Séance.
Hm?
Let's make a deal.
Oh? When did you pick up this trick?
Observe someone, find their weakness, then exploit it using the most cost-effective method.
You taught me that, didn't you?
...Go on.
The Mistresses are willing to give you separate lodging to protect your body, right?
Because you're not capable of keeping your body safe while you're carrying out your tasks...
Correct.
But even in a separate room, if someone like me barges in, you'll still be in grave danger...
So?
So...
Hire me to guard your body.
Miss Séance fiddles with the empty glass and smiles thoughtfully.
Why should I trust you?
How do I know you're not trying to get rid of me?
I need you. Without you, the Mistresses won't think twice about tossing me away.
I thought you were gonna say you're doing this to repay me for saving your life...
We're not like that human woman who came seeking reassurance.
Dolls who are constantly struggling to survive will never be fooled by fanciful words. We can always see the ugly, twisted truth behind the thin façade of illusory goodness.
So you'd rather just tear off this façade and dump a bombshell on me?
I think the transaction will work very much to your benefit, Miss Séance.
Nothing has to change. You don't have to pay me extra, but you will gain more personal safety.
Indeed.
With a grin, Miss Séance fishes out another bottle and glass, then pours some liquor into the two glasses.
I like you. Let's drink to our deal.
Miss Poker picks up both glasses. She opens the window and pours away the liquid mercilessly.
Hey! What the hell?!
While I was inspecting you earlier, I found out that you actually have very low alcohol tolerance. Consuming too much alcohol is very bad for your body.
I... I need this stuff to get into the right headspace for work!
Yeah, I figured as much. From now on, you are only allowed to drink after you're done with a job.
Are you the devil?!
Miss Poker pours two glasses of ginger ale stoically and passes one to Miss Séance.
This is much tastier than your booze. Let's toast with this instead.
I'm already regretting this deal.
Too late.
Miss Poker clinks her glass against Miss Séance's and knocks back her ginger ale.
Ah—that hit the spot!
